title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: Luminescence dissymmetry is largest when the electric and magnetic transition-dipole strengths are comparable and nearly parallel, so magnetic-dipole-allowed, only partly electric-dipole-allowed 4f–4f bands of chiral Ln(III) complexes typically give much larger glum than purely electric-dipole organic emitters.
explanation: From the rotatory-strength and dipole-strength relations, glum scales with 4|μ||m|cosθ/(|μ|^2+|m|^2) and peaks when |μ|/|m| is near 1. Organic enantiomers are stated to fall around 10^-3–10^-2, whereas chiral Ln(III) complexes commonly reach about 0.1–1.45 because 4f–4f emission can be magnetic-dipole and/or forced-electric-dipole allowed. Eu(III) 5D0→7F1 is the textbook magnetic-dipole case.
scope: Chiral luminescent molecules, with emphasis on Ln(III) 4f–4f emission versus organic fluorophores.
conditions: Ideal comparison assumes θ = 0 (cosθ = 1) as plotted in Fig. 3; glum = ±2 is complete circular polarization and 0 is unpolarized emission.
caveats: Oscillator-strength orders (ED much larger than MD) are general estimates, not measured values for every complex.
